title: Full output likelihoods added 0.33 to 1.72 information points in selected small circuits from eight worm maps at release probability 0.5
abstract: We tested whether nonlinear readout can recover site-specific release information lost by linear readout. We used public synaptic site annotations from eight C. elegans maps and a fixed 162-neuron panel. We enumerated all release states for 848 source circuits with 2 to 16 retained sites and at least two targets. In an independent Bernoulli release model with unit effects, full output Fisher information exceeded the best linear value by 0.33 to 1.72 percentage points in equal-source map means at release probability 0.5. Gains were 0.78 to 3.44 points at probability 0.1. A bound based on identical target sets limited even nonlinear readout. The selected circuits contained 6394 of 13487 eligible-panel sites. The two adult maps contributed only 51 and 57 sources. These are exact finite-model calculations, not measured neural coding. Partial coverage, size selection, uniform release probabilities and unit effects limit inference. Code, proof, aggregate scores, input hashes and retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Mean information retained in selected source circuits. Full likelihood gains depend on assumed release probability. Different maps contain different selected sources.

citations.reason: Extends the linear single-site signal test to full discrete output likelihoods; uses its panel and source rules with a new size restriction. No code reused.
